notes: The *have ... in derision* idiom is read as the verb's own light-verb rendering (rule 44), leaving עַל unrepresented under rule 40; giving *in* to עַל was the competing reading, rejected because *in derision* is the complement of *have* rather than a rendering of the Hebrew relation.
לְיָמִים is left wholly unrepresented because the ASV's *younger than I* writes nothing for it.
אֲשֶׁר with its resumptive possessive suffix is one *Whose* unit headed on the relative, exactly as rule 22's closing paragraph directs; the noun keeps its own *fathers*.
